Privacy Policy

Last updated September 2026

Personify keeps everything you put into it on your own phone. There is no account to create, no server to sign in to, and nothing is sent anywhere. This policy exists to say exactly that, and to be specific about the few places your data touches the rest of your device.

What is collected

Nothing is collected. Personify has no analytics, no crash reporting, no advertising, and no way to identify you. It does not know your name unless you type it into a note.

Everything you create — tasks, events, contacts, files, notes, diary entries, money records, savings goals — is written to a database inside the app's own private storage on your phone. Other apps cannot read it. It is not backed up to any service by Personify.

What leaves your phone

Only what you deliberately send. Sharing or exporting something hands it to whichever app you pick from your phone's share sheet — a messaging app, an email app, a cloud drive. From that moment it is governed by that app's rules, not by this one.

Personify makes one kind of network request, and only one: it asks its update server whether a newer version of the app’s own code has been published. That happens when you open the app, when you return to it after several hours, and about once an hour in the background — the same background check that lets a nudge or an announcement reach you while the app is closed. Android decides when those background runs actually happen, and skips them on a low battery or a metered connection.

The request carries the version you are running and nothing else — no account, no identifier, nothing you have written. If a new version exists it is downloaded and used the next time you open the app. On a phone with no connection it fails quietly and nothing changes.

If your phone was set up from Google Play, the Play Store itself also tells the app when a newer version is available on the store, so it can let you know. That check happens on your device through Google Play services; Personify sends nothing to it.

Nothing else goes out. There is no analytics, no crash reporting, and nothing that describes you or what you have written.

Permissions, and what each is for

Notifications — to show reminders and to ring alarms you set. Without it, reminders are silent.

Photos and videos — to let you pick a photo to import, and, if you ask Personify to read a file left in place, to find that item again later. Personify never deletes anything from your gallery, and never browses it on its own; it only sees what you select.

Camera — only while you are taking a photo from inside the app.

Contacts — only if you use the contact import, and only to read the contacts you choose to bring in. Personify does not send your address book anywhere.

Fingerprint or face unlock — used by your phone's own security system to confirm it is you before opening a locked section, or before handing back the shortcut key for your encryption password. Personify never sees your fingerprint or your face; your phone answers yes or no.

Files you leave in place

When you add a file and choose to leave it where it is, Personify stores its location and reads it from there. It does not copy it, move it, or change it. Deleting the entry in Personify leaves your file untouched.

When you choose to keep a copy, Personify copies the file into its own storage and leaves your original completely alone. It has no way to delete a file belonging to another app — Android does not permit that — so after an import it tells you where your original still is, and deleting it is yours to do, in whatever app holds it.

Encryption

If you turn encryption on, the things you lock are scrambled on your phone with a key that only your password can unwrap. Your password is never stored, anywhere, in any form — not on the phone and certainly not off it.

This has one consequence worth stating twice: nobody can recover your locked data without that password. Not you, not this app, not its author. There is no reset, no backdoor, and no support address that can help. That is what makes the lock worth having.

The optional fingerprint shortcut stores a second wrapped copy of the same key in your phone's own keystore, released only after your phone has confirmed it is you. It never stores or reconstructs your password.

Backups and losing your data

Because nothing is stored on a server, uninstalling Personify, wiping your phone, or losing it takes your data with it. Your phone's own backup system may or may not include app data depending on your settings and your manufacturer — Personify does not manage that for you.

If something matters, export it. Notes and diary entries can be exported as documents, and files can be shared out to anywhere you keep backups.

Ratings and nudges

The rating invitation is the only thing in Personify that asks you for anything. Tapping it opens Google Play's own review sheet; Personify learns nothing about what you write there, or whether you wrote anything at all.

Nudges — the occasional note about an unpaid bill or a quiet journal — are worked out on your phone from your own records and scheduled with your phone's own notification system. Nothing about them is sent or received. They can be turned off entirely in Settings.

Children

Personify is a personal organiser with no social features, no messaging and no content from anyone else. It collects nothing from anyone, of any age.

Changes

If a future version starts doing something this policy does not describe, the policy changes with it, in the same update, and the date at the top changes too.

Contact

Questions about this policy, or about the app, can be sent to gnkhars23@gmail.com, or by phone or WhatsApp to +233 54 900 7619.

There is no account to ask about and no data held anywhere that could be handed over, corrected or deleted on request — it is all on your own phone, where you can delete it yourself at any time by removing the item or uninstalling the app.
